title: Identification of a counit cone from an ordinary complementary triangle
statement:
Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal T_Z,\mathcal T_U$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Suppose exact additive functors are supplied with adjunctions $i^*:\mathcal T\rightleftarrows\mathcal T_Z:i_*$, $i_*:\mathcal T_Z\rightleftarrows\mathcal T:i^!$, $j_!:\mathcal T_U\rightleftarrows\mathcal T:j^*$ and $j^*:\mathcal T\rightleftarrows\mathcal T_U:j_*$, where in each displayed pair the left functor is left adjoint (natural Hom bijections, with units and counits satisfying the triangle identities). Suppose $i^*i_*\to1$ and $j^*j_*\to1$ are isomorphisms, $j^*i_*=0$, and for every $M\in\mathcal T$ the ordinary adjunction maps occur in a distinguished triangle $j_!j^*M\to M\to i_*i^*M\to(j_!j^*M)[1]$.

For $K\in\mathcal T$ let $e:i_*i^!K\to K$ be the exceptional counit and $u:K\to j_*j^*K$ the open unit. For any distinguished completion $i_*i^!K\xrightarrow e K\xrightarrow v C\to(i_*i^!K)[1]$, there is a unique map $\beta:C\to j_*j^*K$ satisfying $\beta v=u$, and this map is an isomorphism. Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(i_*P[m],j_*Q)=0$ for every $P,Q,m$.

proof.text: Write $A=i_*i^!K$ and $B=j_*j^*K$. For arbitrary $P\in\mathcal T_Z$, $Q\in\mathcal T_U$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, the adjunction $j^*\dashv j_*$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],j_*Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P[m],Q)=0$, because $j^*i_*=0$ and the functors are exact. The triangle identity for $j^*\dashv j_*$ identifies the adjunct of $u\circ e:A\to B$ with the composite through $j^*A=j^*i_*i^!K=0$, so $u\circ e=0$.
By (TR1) in [def-weil-triangulated-category], complete the exceptional counit $e:A\to K$ to a distinguished triangle $A\xrightarrow{e}K\xrightarrow{v}C\xrightarrow{w}A[1]$.

Apply exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(-,B)$ to this triangle, using [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact]. Since $u e=0$, there is $\beta:C\to B$ with $\beta v=u$. If $\beta'$ is another such map, $(\beta-\beta')v=0$, so the same exactness gives $\beta-\beta'=h w$ for some $h:A[1]\to B$. The orthogonality in Step 1 makes $h=0$, proving uniqueness.

Closed orthogonality of $C$ and $B$. Let $Q\in\mathcal T_Z$. The bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,i^!K)\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,K)$ of $i_*\dashv i^!$ is $g\mapsto e\circ i_*g$, and $g\mapsto i_*g$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-counit-iso-right-fully-faithful] for $i^*\dashv i_*$ with invertible counit; hence $e\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,K)$ is bijective for every $Q$. Applying the inverse shift and $i_*(Q[-1])\cong(i_*Q)[-1]$, also $e[1]\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,A[1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,K[1])$ is injective. Let $f:i_*Q\to C$. The twice-rotated triangle $C\xrightarrow wA[1]\xrightarrow{-e[1]}K[1]$ (TR2) has zero composite by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](i), so $e[1]\circ(wf)=0$ and $wf=0$. By (ii) of that node for the rotated triangle $K\xrightarrow vC\xrightarrow wA[1]$, $f=vb$ with $b:i_*Q\to K$; write $b=eh$; then $f=veh=0$ by (i). So $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,C)=0$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,B)=0$ by Step 1, for all $Q$ (all shifts included, as $i_*P[m]\cong i_*(P[m])$). Now let $X$ be any object with $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,X)=0$ for all $Q$, and $M\in\mathcal T$ with its triangle $j_!j^*M\xrightarrow{c}M\xrightarrow{\iota}i_*i^*M\xrightarrow{\delta}$. If $fc=0$ then $f=g\iota$ with $g\in\operatorname{Hom}(i_*i^*M,X)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact](i). The triangle $(i_*i^*M)[-1]\xrightarrow{-\delta[-1]}j_!j^*M\xrightarrow cM\xrightarrow\iota i_*i^*M$ is distinguished by TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], its rotation being the given one; for $a:j_!j^*M\to X$, $a\circ(-\delta[-1])\in\operatorname{Hom}(i_*(i^*M[-1]),X)=0$, so $a=fc$ by (i). Thus $f\mapsto fc$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(M,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*M,X)$, natural in $X$.

source.place: Existence, second and third paragraphs: apply $Lj^*$ and $Ri^!$ to the counit triangle and use $Ri^!C=0$, $Lj^*u$ invertible

proof.text: Reduction to the open side. For $X\in\{C,B\}$ compose the bijection of the previous step with the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*M,X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j^*M,j^*X)$ of $j_!\dashv j^*$; both are natural in $X$, so under them $\beta\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}(M,C)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,B)$ becomes $j^*\beta\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}(j^*M,j^*C)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j^*M,j^*B)$. It suffices that $j^*\beta$ is invertible. The exact functor $j^*$ carries the cone triangle to a distinguished triangle $j^*A\to j^*K\xrightarrow{j^*v}j^*C\to(j^*A)[1]$ with $j^*A=j^*i_*i^!K=0$ and so $(j^*A)[1]=0$. For every $W\in\mathcal T_U$, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](ii), applied to this triangle and to its rotation (TR2), makes $j^*v\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}(W,j^*K)\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,j^*C)$ injective and surjective, so $j^*v$ is an isomorphism by [lem-coef-joyal-homset-iso-detection]. The triangle identity of $j^*\dashv j_*$ gives $\varepsilon_{j^*K}\circ j^*u=1$ with $\varepsilon:j^*j_*\to1$ invertible, so $j^*u$ is invertible. From $j^*\beta\circ j^*v=j^*u$, $j^*\beta$ is an isomorphism, hence $\operatorname{Hom}(M,\beta)$ is bijective for every $M\in\mathcal T$.

source.place: Existence, second and third paragraphs: apply $Lj^*$ and $Ri^!$ to the counit triangle and use $Ri^!C=0$, $Lj^*u$ invertible

proof.text: The bijectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}(M,\beta)$ for every object $M$ implies that $\beta$ is an isomorphism by the Yoneda Hom-set criterion [lem-coef-joyal-homset-iso-detection]. Thus the unique comparison $\beta:C\to j_*j^*K$ is invertible and satisfies $\beta v=u$, as required.
